results.summary_before: This asynchronous FIFO enables data transfer between two clock domains using separate read and write clocks. It uses Gray-coded pointers for synchronization and provides full and empty flags. The design can be fully simulated without external hardware, but on an FPGA, LEDs or UART may be used to display status. It is a standard implementation of a clock-domain-crossing FIFO.

results.summary_before: This programmable threshold voltage comparator compares an external reference voltage with one of eight selectable threshold levels, seven fixed and one user-defined. It uses a resistor ladder and passgates controlled by a decoder, and outputs a digital high when the reference exceeds the threshold. Testing requires a 1.8V supply and input voltages up to 1.8V, with a maximum switching frequency of 100 kHz. The design is analog-intensive and provides a flexible voltage sensing capability.

results.summary_before: This is a 16-bit CPU based on the HACK architecture, containing D and A registers, a program counter, an ALU with 18 operations, and SPI master logic. Because the chip lacks on-chip memory, instructions and data are fetched from an external SPI RAM one 16-bit word at a time, and a second SPI port provides debug access to the D register, A register, program counter and FSM state. The design targets a Microchip 23XX512 SPI RAM and a microcontroller for debugging, and it matches the SPI Pmod pinout. It is notable for fitting a working CPU into a single tile by serializing memory access.

results.summary_before: An ALU for the five operators of the INTERCAL programming language, including unary AND, OR, XOR, interleave, and select. It features two 32-bit registers and supports reading and writing bytes via address and selector pins. The design is intended for educational and novelty purposes, with extensive documentation and test cases. It can be used without external hardware, though a microcontroller is recommended for driving inputs and reading outputs.
